answer: A marketplace for lantern design, karst mapping and zenith tracking requires each agent identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding. Provably conflicting signed commitments trigger forfeiture of that bond. Creating 1,000 fake bidders therefore ties up $100,000, sacrifices its alternative returns and risks losing it outright. Cheap key generation no longer means cheap participation, though a wealthy attacker can still buy access.
